title: Stacks, queues, and the final command catalogue
goal: Choose LIFO or FIFO, check emptiness, and connect module skills in a verifiable project.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.linked-lists, cpp.standard-sequences. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: LIFO and FIFO
paragraphs: std::stack<T> from <stack> provides last in, first out: the most recently pushed element is removed first. std::queue<T> from <queue> provides first in, first out: the earliest element is processed first. These are access disciplines, not physical representations.

Both adapt an underlying suitable container. A teaching queue does not require reimplementing a linked list. Justify the choice by ordering, size, and operations; arbitrary indexed access is not part of these interfaces.

sections.title: Operations and preconditions
paragraphs: push adds an element, empty checks absence, and size gives the count. stack top reads the top; queue front reads the beginning and back the end. These read operations require a nonempty adapter.

pop removes an element but returns no value. Read the required value with top/front before pop. Do not retain a reference to the removed element. Calling pop on empty is not a valid way to discover emptiness.

sections.title: Same input, different order
paragraphs: Read top and front only from nonempty adapters.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.
Trace state after each significant operation and identify the established preconditions.
Run the source, compare stdout and exit code, then check the additional cases.

sections.title: Undo as state history
paragraphs: For a small catalogue, save the previous validated state in a stack before a successful mutation. undo restores top and removes it. A rejected command must not add history, or undo would depend on user errors.

A whole-state copy is simple but uses memory proportional to record count per step. Inverse operations are more compact but harder to justify. The project uses bounded snapshots and explicit record and command limits.

sections.title: Queueing and execution
paragraphs: A parser validates command syntax and queues the command. The executor reads front and applies domain checks to the current state. A syntactically valid command can still be rejected because stock is insufficient at execution time.

Order matters: add followed by remove can differ from the reverse order. Process the finite queue sequentially and print one result per command for reproducibility. Concurrency and blocking queues are outside this lesson.

sections.title: History only for successful updates
paragraphs: Push the previous state before a successful update and pop it when undoing.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.
Trace state after each significant operation and identify the established preconditions.
Run the source, compare stdout and exit code, then check the additional cases.

sections.title: Project integration
paragraphs: The final project uses a record vector, a queue of typed commands, a stack of snapshots for undo, contracted functions, and text import/export. The previous lesson’s list remains a separate learning artifact with a justified comparison rather than an unnecessary catalogue dependency.

Split the work into parsing, domain operations, report formatting, and main. Build the application and test driver separately. Assessment includes design explanations and original tests; a working reference does not prove learner mastery.

sections.title: Order tests and final defence
paragraphs: The lab supplies identical values to a stack and queue and compares reverse and original order. Test empty, singleton, and duplicate inputs. Guard every top/front with empty and read before each pop.

For the project, demonstrate rejection without mutation, two undos, empty history, a malformed file, and a saved-report roundtrip. In the defence explain ownership, bounds, and complexity, then change one requirement and add a test. This provides evidence of independent understanding.

practice.title: Laboratory: Stacks, queues, and the final command catalogue
practice.task: Read n in 0…100 and n integers in -1000…1000. Fill a stack and queue, then print their removal orders on two lines. Empty input data produces two empty lines.
criteria: The contract matches the task and defines units, empty input, and extra data.
Every published case matches and two explained original tests are included.
Removal order is part of the domain contract.
Do not add history for a rejected command. Do not read front/top on an empty adapter.
Source, actual output, exit code, and a justified complexity explanation are preserved.

Start from the scaffold, implement the valid path, then add boundary checks.
For every reference case, independently write the expectation before running; keep stdout and exit code.
Add two original cases including one rejection; explain the result without consulting the reference.
Preserve source, a result table, and a short cost-and-limit analysis.

requirements: catalog.txt: exact NEXUS_CATALOG_V1 header followed by at most 10 id stock lines; id is unique in 1…1000, stock is in 0…1000.
stdin: at most 50 lines of 200 bytes; add id amount, remove id amount, undo, list, export. Blank lines and trailing fields are invalid.
Parse every command before execution; on syntax failure print only invalid without partial execution.
add/remove with amount in 0…1000 apply only to an existing id and retain stock in 0…1000; rejected commands do not change history. A successful zero-amount command still records a snapshot.
undo restores the prior snapshot and prints undone; empty history prints empty-history. list preserves input order and prints space-separated id:stock fields.
export creates catalog-out.txt in the same format and prints exported, or write-error on failure. missing means catalog.txt is absent; an unknown version or malformed catalogue is invalid.
Each run gets a fresh FS. Check the output contents, explicitly save permitted text into the VFS, and run a fresh import from that file.

The portfolio includes 18 labs and three cumulative practica. Their respective artifacts demonstrate matrices, span, variant, and ownership; do not add unnecessary structures to the catalogue merely to tick off topics.
milestones: A. Contract, record model, manual expectations, and a unit driver.
B. Parser, operations, and queue; rejections preserve state.
C. Undo stack, versioned format, and export; roundtrip verification.
D. Multifile build, complete case set, and a mini-defence including a changed requirement.
walkthrough: Starting at 1:5, add 1 3 produces 1:8 with a 1:5 snapshot. remove 1 8 produces 1:0 with a 1:8 snapshot. undo restores 1:8, and export must contain that state.
Bounds allow up to 10 records and 50 snapshots of 10 records. Search is O(n), queue processing is sequential; worst-case domain work is O(commands*records), with O(commands*records) history storage.
Compare vector with the teaching list, but do not add a list without a reason. Build the driver below as a separate main with the same domain.cpp and format.cpp.
